source.title: WriteBinaryFile and ReadWriteFile node tests fail on macOS

labels.name: status:in-linear
labels.description: Issue or PR is now in Linear

source.body:
### Bug Description

On a clean checkout of `master`, two node tests fail on macOS:

- `nodes/WriteBinaryFile/test/WriteBinaryFile.test.ts`
- `nodes/Files/ReadWriteFile/test/ReadWriteFile.test.ts`

Both fail the same way: the write node returns no output.

```
AssertionError: Equality failed for "nodes/WriteBinaryFile/test/WriteBinaryFile.workflow.json" at node "Write Binary File": expected [ null ] to deeply equal [ [ { …(2) } ] ]
```

Both tests write into `NodeTestHarness.temporaryDir`, which is built from `os.tmpdir()`. On macOS that's `/var/folders/...`, and `/var` is a symlink to `/private/var`. Both tests also stub `fs.promises.realpath` to return the path unchanged, so the path is never resolved. The file system helpers then refuse to write, because the parent path has a symlinked component (`assertNoSymlinkInPath` in `file-system-helper-functions.ts`).

It's a test problem, not a product one. With the real `realpath`, `/var/...` resolves to `/private/var/...` first, and both tests pass on macOS once the stub is removed. CI runs on Linux, where the temp dir isn't behind a symlink, so it never shows up there.

### To Reproduce

On macOS:

```sh
cd packages/nodes-base
npx vitest run nodes/WriteBinaryFile/test/WriteBinaryFile.test.ts nodes/Files/ReadWriteFile/test/ReadWriteFile.test.ts
# Tests  2 failed (2)

TMPDIR=$(realpath "$TMPDIR") npx vitest run nodes/WriteBinaryFile/test/WriteBinaryFile.test.ts nodes/Files/ReadWriteFile/test/ReadWriteFile.test.ts
# Tests  2 passed (2)
```

### Expected behavior

The node tests pass on macOS as they do on Linux. The harness can create its temp dir under `realpathSync(os.tmpdir())`, which fixes every test that writes there without changing the existing `realpath` stubs. I have that fix ready, with a regression test, and will link a PR.

### Debug Info

Not applicable: this is the unit test suite run from source, not a running instance.

### Operating System

macOS 27.3 (arm64)

### n8n Version

master at 327518f80b (2.49.0)

### Node.js Version

24.5.0

### Database

SQLite (default)

### Execution mode

main (default)

### Hosting

self hosted

comments.author: goutham-valugula
comments.text: The two tests stub `fs.promises.realpath` to return the input unchanged, while `NodeTestHarness.temporaryDir` is created under `os.tmpdir()`. On macOS, `/var/folders/...` traverses the `/var` symlink, so the file-system helper’s symlink check rejects the write; the current helper resolves paths with `realpath` before that check. Resolving `tmpdir()` before `mkdtempSync` in the harness looks like a focused fix that keeps the test stubs and covers other harness tests writing into the same directory. A regression assertion for the canonical temp path would help guard this across macOS runners.
